title: Mariner on-prem engagement prep — runbook & weekly sync notes
content:
Meeting: Mariner on-prem engagement — weekly sync prep
Date (for this doc): 2026-03-10
Owner (notes): Ashley Park (runbook owner)
Recent context: Customer signed PO for private deployment w/ dedicated NUC-like appliances in their colo. Still on target for initial staging window week of 2026-03-22 but infra team requested a more detailed smoke test/runbook before handoff.

Goals for the sync:
- Confirm staging window + change window alignment with Mariner (UTC-7)
- Validate network/cert prechecks are complete (IP allocations, firewall rules, KMS reachability)
- Walk through runbook (smoke tests, rollback criteria, monitoring hooks) and assign owners for each step
- Surface any outstanding blockers and get commitments to unblock by next sync

Attendees to invite (proposed):
- Tom Reyes (Mariner infra lead)
- Ashley Park (Redwood engagement lead)
- Kevin Liu (Redwood SRE)
- Maya Patel (Redwood security/KMS lead)
- Priya Singh (Redwood solutions eng)
- Mariner: NetOps + App owner (ask Tom to include)

Agenda (35–45m):
1) 3m quick status: what changed since last week (PO, IPs, cable rack ETA)
2) 8m runbook walkthrough (owner annotations and time estimates)
3) 7m prechecks & gating (KMS, DNS, certs)
4) 7m smoke test and success criteria (token-level perf, end-to-end generation, auth)
5) 5m rollback & fallback (how we fail open to hosted API if problem)
6) 5m blockers/commitments + next meeting scheduling

Runbook summary (high level) — rough draft checklist (to be expanded into confluence):
- Pre-deploy checklist (owner: Tom/Mariner + Kevin)
  - Confirm rack/cable labelled and power tested (Mariner)
  - IP/Subnet allocations provisioned and shared with Redwood (Mariner)
  - Firewall rules (outbound to Redwood control plane endpoints) whitelisted (Mariner)
  - KMS/HSM connectivity test: mutual TLS handshake & test key wrap (Maya + Mariner)
  - NTP sync and time drift < 500ms (Kevin)
